frontier.hypothesis: One of the four sibling functions with the same descriptor-plus-hole layout (func_8006F97C, 12 bytes, identical to this one; func_80069F80 and func_8006A1A0, 20 bytes; func_80070188, 36 bytes) has a target that genuinely WRITES into its hole, which would name the object the original programmer declared there and convert the whole family to ordinary C at once.
frontier.mechanism: The hole must be an aggregate or address-taken decl (stmt.c:3357-3364); a sibling whose target contains stores into it identifies the type and its truthful role, and all five functions share the func_8007352C descriptor idiom and the func_80069898 rect idiom, so the declaration block is very likely copy-pasted between them.
frontier.next_probe: Forensics modality: for each of the four siblings, map every store/load — including those made through a computed base register, which tmp/grind/func_8006DD94/s1/census.py deliberately does not follow — onto the sp frame, and look for any write landing between the 0x2C descriptor and the rect. Extend census.py to track `addiu $rX,$sp,N` bases and their subsequent stores.

frontier.hypothesis: The 8 bytes belong to an address-taken scalar or a small aggregate that IS used, and the traffic it would emit is absent from the target because the original's uses are all in a path this reconstruction folded away (for example a second rect built on a branch, as func_800720FC really does).
frontier.mechanism: t5_addrof and v4_inner_plus_used_arr both reach the target frame with a used object; they were rejected only because they add sp-relative traffic. If the object's stores coincide with insns already in the target, the frame closes with no dead declaration at all.
frontier.next_probe: Re-derive modality: take the target's 117 insns and check whether ANY of them can be read as a store into sp+0x44..0x4F under a different register/offset attribution (e.g. a store through a base register set up earlier); if not, this hypothesis dies and the residual is provably a declaration with zero uses.

frontier.hypothesis: The residual cannot be closed by any construct that also lowers the honest floor, so the correct disposition once the ladder is spent is rotation — not a pad grant.
frontier.mechanism: H10 shows the sandbox strips every unwritten filler; the Judge (2026-09-10 05:59) refused interior pads and the frozen volatile-pad family is form-constrained to LEADING holes, which cannot occur here because the descriptor already sits at the bottom of the vars region (sp+0x18, immediately above the 24-byte arg area).
frontier.next_probe: Only after frontier item 1 is spent: in escalation modality, file the proof-of-foreclosure record in docs/grind/decisions.md with floor 21 (so the >5 'LADDER EXHAUSTED (non-endgame residual, floor 21): ROTATED' title, not the standing-ruling title) and return owner-gated.
